architectures.reason: No qualified submerged pod interface; dry-side evidence not transferable

hypothesis.question: Can service components be replaced while retaining rotor and generator datums, with independent shaft support and verified local access?
hypothesis.comparator: Same maintenance task using a one-piece interface requiring shaft or machine withdrawal; compare both dry-PTO architectures fairly.
hypothesis.mechanism: Separate component renewal from whole-cartridge retrieval to investigate reduced disassembly and realignment burden.
hypothesis.falsifier: Required support, hub/key travel, radial removal or tool/guard access cannot fit; or added hardware and water-system burdens erase any measured benefit.
necessary_evidence: qualified load envelope and torsional review
shaft geometry and independent axial/radial support in each service state
dimensioned disassembly motion for selected components
matched measured service tasks and installed cost
metered pumping and other auxiliary demand without double counting

prohibitions: No measured service-time, efficiency or cost advantage
No wildlife safety or permitting approval
No replacement of the synthetic retrieval or energy inputs with catalogue geometry
